OCTOBER, 1948. Peak Load Problem this Winter

IN February, 1948, a Committee, under Sir Andrew Clow, K.C.S.I., C.I.E., was set up to examine and report on “the practicability of installing any instrument by means of which maximum demand and consumption at different times of the day by domestic and non-industrial consumers may be measured and controlled” and “the possibility of securing a reduction of the peak demand on the electricity supply system either by the use of any such instruments or by alterations in the tariff for domestic and non-industrial consumers or by a combination of those methods.”

The Electrical Association for Women was among those who gave evidence, and the Report published in July specifically recommended that the utmost use should be made of the E.A.W. in bringing home to householders the need for reducing load at peak load times and in teaching methods for doing so.
